decks.name: LeetCode #22 - Generate Parentheses
decks.description: Generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses for n pairs

cards.question: Generate Parentheses: Given n pairs of parentheses, write a function to generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses.

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.explanation: Generate all possible strings of length 2n containing only parentheses, then filter valid ones. Use DFS to recursively build strings by appending either open or close parenthesis at each step. When string reaches length 2n, validate by tracking balance counter. Counter increments for open parenthesis, decrements for close. Invalid if counter goes negative or non-zero at end. Generates 2^(2n) strings and validates each. Very inefficient but conceptually simple. O(2^(2n)*n) time complexity.

solutions.timeDescription: Generate all 2^(2n) possible strings of length 2n, each validation takes O(n) time to check balance
solutions.spaceDescription: Recursion stack depth O(2n), each call stores string of length up to 2n, stores all generated strings
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given n=3: Generate all 2^6=64 strings. Examples: '((()))' valid (balance stays 0-3, ends 0), '(((' invalid (ends 3 not 0), '())' incomplete (length 3 not 6), ')))(((' invalid (balance goes negative at start). Valid ones: '((()))', '(()())', '(())()', '()(())', '()()()'. Filter reduces 64 strings to 5 valid combinations.

solutions.name: Backtracking
solutions.explanation: Only generate valid parentheses strings using backtracking with constraints. Track count of open and closed parentheses used so far. Base case when both counts equal n, add current string to result. Can only add open parenthesis if openN less than n. Can only add close parenthesis if closedN less than openN (maintains validity). Use stack to build string character by character, backtrack by popping. Prunes invalid branches early, only explores valid paths. O(4^n/sqrt(n)) time which is nth Catalan number. Much more efficient than brute force.

solutions.timeDescription: Generates nth Catalan number of valid sequences, which is approximately 4^n divided by n^(3/2), only explores valid branches
solutions.spaceDescription: Recursion stack depth O(n) for 2n characters, stack array stores up to 2n characters, output space not counted
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given n=3: Start backtrack(0,0). Add '(': backtrack(1,0). Add '(': backtrack(2,0). Add '(': backtrack(3,0). Now can only add ')': backtrack(3,1), then backtrack(3,2), then backtrack(3,3) adds '((()))'. Backtrack explores all valid paths. Tree prunes invalid branches like adding ')' when closedN>=openN. Result: ['((()))', '(()())', '(())()', '()(())', '()()()'].

solutions.name: Dynamic Programming
solutions.explanation: Build solutions bottom-up using previously computed results. Key insight: for k pairs, each valid string has form '(' + left + ')' + right, where left uses i pairs and right uses k-i-1 pairs (totaling k-1 pairs inside/after first pair). Create dp array where dp[k] contains all valid strings with k pairs. Base case dp[0] contains empty string. For each k from 0 to n, iterate through all splits i from 0 to k-1. Combine all strings from dp[i] as left part with all strings from dp[k-i-1] as right part. Same O(4^n/sqrt(n)) time complexity as backtracking but iterative approach. Demonstrates Catalan number recurrence relation.
